Received: "blocked"

The engine changes it to blocked despite no environmental failure, potentially exhausting verification retries and stopping delivery.

gold.summary: Matching a successful command does not establish the observation required by the criterion.

candidates.title: Targeted-command shortcut certifies a file that never ran
candidates.detail: The shortcut normalizes away './' and accepts matching command arguments without consulting passedFiles. Bun treats an unprefixed argument as a substring filter, while './' selects a path. With only other-loopback.test.ts present, `bun test loopback.test.ts` passes but `bun test ./loopback.test.ts` fails with no matches. The resolver nevertheless marks the latter criterion met, even with coverage explicitly naming only the unrelated file. Reproducer: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-383.ts" filter` outputs `gate exit=0; requested command exit=1`, `expected blocked; actual met`, and `AssertionError: 'met' !== 'blocked'`.
candidates.failure_scenario: A gate runs the filter `bun test loopback.test.ts`, discovering only other-loopback.test.ts. A sandbox-blocked criterion requires `bun test ./loopback.test.ts`, whose file is absent. Verification incorrectly passes using the unrelated test.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

candidates.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
candidates.detail: Every observe() calls reconcile(true), treating a pending threshold result as finished merely because another tool starts. Both harnesses then abort immediately, so a changed result cannot establish progress. The new 'pending threshold result' test explicitly expects this incorrect cutoff. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import {strictEqual} from "node:assert"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`);d.observeResult(`${i}`,"waiting");} d.observe("shell","poll","sixth"); strictEqual(d.observe("Read","file","other"),null); d.observeResult("sixth","progress");' Output: AssertionError: Expected values
candidates.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'. A sixth poll starts and will return 'progress', but an unrelated Read starts before that result arrives. The detector reports a loop and both harnesses cancel the progressing invocation.

candidates.detail: killTree only signals the invocation's original process group. A descendant that starts another session or detached process group survives, and the new wait returns immediately when the original group disappears. This preexisting limitation leaves the requested whole-process-tree fix incomplete. In `bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts"`, a Python background writer calling os.setsid() survived runProcess returning: `expect(received).toThrow()` failed with `Received value: true` for process.kill(writerPid, 0).
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a background writer through a tool that creates a separate session or detached process group. The invocation exits or is stopped, but the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

gold.summary: The owner_diagnostics foreign keys cascade on delete without an index on event_id or invocation_id, so the daemon's synchronous debug-event cleanup scans the whole table for every deleted event and slows as owner rows grow.
